drivingQuestion: Which reading of the mishna's name is correct?
outcomeNote: Abaye's proof is rejected and the dilemma is left open without a formal תיקו

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: ״בֵּית יַעְזֵק״ תְּנַן, אוֹ ״בֵּית יָזֵק״ תְּנַן? ״בֵּית יַעְזֵק״ תְּנַן — לִישָּׁנָא מְעַלְּיָא הוּא, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְעַזְּקֵהוּ וַיְסַקְּלֵהוּ״, אוֹ דִלְמָא ״בֵּית יָזֵק״ תְּנַן — לִישָּׁנָא דְצַעֲרָא הוּא, כְּדִכְתִיב: ״וְהוּא אָסוּר בָּאזִיקִּים״?
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: What is the correct reading of the mishna? Did «we learn: Beit Ya’zek, or» did «we learn: Beit Yazek?» The Gemara explains the difference between these two versions. «Did we learn: Beit Ya’zek,» which is «an lofty term,» indicating that it was a fine place where the witnesses had a pleasant experience, «as it is written: “And he dug it [vaye’azzekehu] and cleared it of stones”» (Isaiah 5:2), which shows that the root a-z-k denotes improvement? «Or perhaps we learned: Beit Yazek,» which «is a term of distress,» reflecting the fact that the witnesses who arrived there on Shabbat were not permitted to move from there all day, «as it is written: “And he was bound with chains [bazikim]”» (Jeremiah 40:1).

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, תָּא שְׁמַע: סְעוּדוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין לָהֶם שָׁם, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ רְגִילִים לָבוֹא. דִּלְמָא תַּרְתֵּי הֲווֹ עָבְדִי בְּהוּ.
segments.en: «Abaye said: Come» and «hear» the mishna: «They would prepare great feasts for them there, so that they would be accustomed to come» and submit their testimony. This indicates that the witnesses were made welcome, in accordance with the name Beit Ya’zek. The Gemara rejects this argument: «Perhaps they performed two» practices «for them,» i.e., they provided feasts but they also restricted their movement. Therefore, there is no proof from the mishna for this version of the name.
